text:
COP fell barely 0.07% today to $134.10, essentially flat—the real story is the 5.34% jump over the past two weeks, driven by oil prices and geopolitical shifts. Crude has climbed sharply (U.S. oil at $96.24/barrel, world oil at $125.44), and ConocoPhillips, as a major oil producer, benefits directly when prices rise. The past week's gains also reflect uncertainty premium: threats to Middle Eastern shipping from Iran-backed Houthis and new U.S. military involvement could tighten global oil supply, pushing prices higher and boosting producer margins.

The longer backdrop adds complexity. Trump's reported diesel deal with Putin and talk of an "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine initially looked like they might ease supply pressures and cap prices—which would hurt oil producers. But the reality on the ground—refinery damage across Eastern Europe and the Middle East, plus Houthi disruptions—means global oil remains constrained, keeping prices elevated. For a producer like ConocoPhillips, that constraint is favorable, even if the political noise around sanctions and ceasefires creates day-to-day chop.
